sections.name: tools
sections.text:
lookup[name]: returns the fact sheet of a model, e.g. lookup[BERT base]
  calculate[expression]: evaluates arithmetic, e.g. calculate[3 * (4 + 5)]
  finish[answer]: gives the final answer

sections.name: rule
sections.text: After each Action, wait for the Observation. Look up every number you use; do not answer from memory.

sections.name: worked example
sections.text:
Example
Question: How many numbers are in the token embedding matrix of BERT base?
Thought 1: The matrix has one row per vocabulary token and one column per model dimension. I need both sizes.
Action 1: lookup[BERT base]
Observation 1: BERT base (Google, 2018): 12 layers, 12 attention heads per layer, d_model 768, MLP width 3072, vocabulary 30,522 WordPiece tokens, 110M parameters.
Thought 2: The vocabulary has 30,522 tokens and d_model is 768, so I multiply them.
Action 2: calculate[30522 * 768]
Observation 2: 23440896
Thought 3: The matrix holds 23,440,896 numbers.
Action 3: finish[23,440,896]

steps.text:

steps.text:

Action 3: calculate[32 - 12]

Thought 4: The difference is 20.
